title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection thresholds and rollout guards for performance regressions
author: Arjun Gupta
release_notes: Improves automatic detection of latency and throughput regressions with adaptive thresholds; tightens rollout guards to reduce noisy canary aborts; adds perf-canary smoke CI and dashboard updates.
description: Context: Our continuous performance canary sometimes produces noisy aborts when traffic patterns shift or when distributional changes create transient variance. This leads to unnecessary rollbacks that impact rollout velocity. Goal: Reduce false-positive canary aborts while preserving sensitivity to real regressions. Summary: Introduces an adaptive threshold estimator that updates detection thresholds based on stable-window statistics, adds an alert suppression window to avoid aborts caused by transient spikes, and strengthens rollout guards to prefer degraded-but-live fallbacks instead of immediate aborts for non-critical regressions. Also adds unit tests, a perf-smoke job in canary-lab CI, and a dashboard update for the new metrics. Checklist: - Implement adaptive threshold estimator - Add suppression window and config knobs - Update rollout guard behavior and runbook - Add unit/integration tests - Add perf-smoke CI pipeline - Update dashboards and docs Changeset: code changes in detector and guard logic, tests, CI pipeline, dashboard JSON, and docs. Motivation: reduce customer impact from spurious rollbacks while keeping strong regression detection guarantees, improving SLO stability for serving.
commits: fix(perf-canary): correct anomaly window size calculation
feat(guards): add alert suppression window and fallback policy
test(perf-canary): add unit tests for threshold edge cases
ci(canary-lab): add perf-canary smoke job to pipeline
docs(perf-canary): update rollout guard runbook and dashboard notes

Sofia Alvarez: The fallback policy looks good but add trace markers so ops can correlate canary->fallback events. — Arjun: Added trace/span attributes and updated dashboard to surface these events.
Liam O'Connor: Confirmed that the new estimator doesn't regress on our historical 6-month perf baseline. Left a small nit on naming. — Arjun: Nit addressed in commit 4.
Ops/CI: perf-smoke passes locally; scheduling in canary-lab added and green in CI run 2026-02-25.
high_level_summary: Adaptive thresholds + suppression window to reduce noisy canary aborts; safer rollout guard defaults and improved observability; CI/perf smoke coverage added.
